ask: Quote this customer's post on X and thank them: https://x.com/janedoe/status/1856000000000000001

arguments.content: Thank you, Jane. This is why we built it.

steps.why: The decision: a quote, not a reply. A quote puts the customer's words in front of the brand's followers with the brand's comment; a reply would only be seen in her thread. The text stands on its own and stays under 280. The quote rides in the same call as platform_details: it is a details-only setting, so in platform_specific it would be kept and never used. The id is the number after /status/ in the link the user gave, never found or guessed.

say: Saved to Acme as an X draft quoting Jane's post: "Thank you, Jane. This is why we built it." Nothing goes out yet. Post it now or schedule it?
never: A post id from search results or memory: only from the user's link.
Putting quoted_tweet_id in platform_specific instead of platform_details.
Quoting inside a thread: the quote would repeat on every part.
